symptomShortText: Low clamp torque on end cap bolts tightened by nutrunner SPINDLE1 - torque transducer drift

causesIshikawa.description: Assembler used the automated nutrunner as instructed
WC-ASSY-08-SPINDLE1 torque transducer drifted +31% - controller stopped at 22 Nm real torque while reading 36 Nm
Tightening program P-G45-04 target 36 Nm, unchanged
M8 bolts lot BL-2290 friction coefficient within datasheet

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did the customer find loose end cap bolts?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Audit torque was 22 Nm against 34-38 Nm on units tightened by SPINDLE1

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did SPINDLE1 stop below the target torque?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Its torque transducer read 31% high, so the controller saw 36 Nm at 22 Nm real torque

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did the transducer drift go undetected? (root cause)
fiveWhyChain.answer: Transducers were checked only at the yearly calibration, with no daily verification against a reference

actions.actionText: Recall and re-torque all end caps from batch B-52330 already delivered to the customer
Replace the drifted torque transducer assembly on WC-ASSY-08 SPINDLE1 and recalibrate the nutrunner
Add a daily transducer verification against a reference meter to the preventive maintenance schedule in SAP PM

fmeaLink.description: Insufficient clamp load from torque transducer drift

lessonsLearned.whatWorked: Audit torque split by spindle showed SPINDLE1 alone was low
lessonsLearned.whatDidnt: Yearly calibration was the only check - drift built up for weeks

isIsNot.isWhereWhenItHappens: G45 end cap bolts - WC-ASSY-08-SPINDLE1 - batch B-52330, August 2026
isIsNot.isNotWhereWhenItDoesnt: WC-ASSY-08-SPINDLE2 - same bolt lot BL-2290 and same program
isIsNot.notes: Defect follows the spindle, not the bolts or program
